function.arguments: {"research_topic":"Investigate the Wirecard and Jan Marsalek public-fraud trail using only evidence available through the benchmark tools. Build a source-cited evidence dossier, returning the exact source IDs supplied by the tools and no externally supplied facts or citations. Cover five separate strands and their chronology: (1) Wirecard AG’s public company statements, annual reports, ad hoc disclosures, and other investor-facing representations; (2) audit findings, qualifications, warnings, limitations, unresolved uncertainty, and what auditors did or did not establish; (3) the reported or alleged disappearance of cash, trustee accounts, bank confirmations, and the status of relevant funds or accounts; (4) supervisory, regulatory, governmental, prosecutorial, parliamentary, and other institutional actions, omissions, failures, or disputed assessments; and (5) Jan Marsalek’s disappearance, last documented role/events, and only evidence-supported links—if any—to the broader chronology. For every item, distinguish established documentary fact from allegation, assessment, inference, disputed account, and unknown. Extract dates, actors, entities, events, claims, relationships, and contradictions only when directly supported by returned sources. Explain causal or evidentiary links conservatively and flag absent evidence. Structure the response so it can support a final Markdown report and a JSON object with exactly arrays named findings, claims, reasoning_steps, and contradictions. Each finding should be representable with question, answer, supporting_entities, source_references; each claim with claim and source_references; each reasoning step with id, conclusion, premise_entities, premise_relations; and each contradiction with contradiction_id, description, source_references. Do not invent source IDs, facts, dates, motives, relationship names, or conclusions."}
function.name: ConductResearch
